text:
Ian Moore has made the most of four games. He is playing 17 and a half minutes a night, up from under 14 last season, and has two goals and three points. The late goal in Saturday's 3-2 loss came in Utah, where he was born.

Four games is the definition of a small sample, and his goals far outrun his chances: two on about half an expected goal (expected goals measure the quality of chances). But there is a real player here. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 91st percentile at taking chances away last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him getting to the dangerous ice in front of the net more than most defensemen and joining the rush on 31% of his shots, against 17% for a typical defenseman. A Harvard product and a third-round pick in 2020, he is 24. Our range has him around 20 points if the role sticks. Watch the minutes once the Ducks get healthy.
